lines.t: Wind's turned. Smells like heather and rain from the north — that's Brackenridge weather. Take a coat.
Best view on Thistledown Way, this. See that big dark crown on the horizon, north? That's the Great Hollow Tree in Murmurwood.
When the wind's right you can hear it hum from here. Today it's… humming wrong. Like it's got something stuck in its throat.
Gustlings love this hill. If your kin can fly, bring it up here on a breezy day. It'll never want to leave.
Still here. Still no bites. I've decided that's the fish being polite.
Shh. The fish are listening. Or they were, before the stone went quiet. Now they're just sulking under the islet.
See that carved stone at the water's edge? Old boatmen's glyph. A kin with a water voice can sing up stepping-stones to the islet.
Don't dawdle out there, mind. They sink again after a minute. I've lost two hats that way.
